subject: Post-demo: NovusTech inference probe & quality asks
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@novustech.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: NovusTech QA <qa@novustech.com>
Date: 2028-09-10 09:12 -0700
Subject: Post-demo follow-up + asks

Ben — thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap and the things we'd like Redwood to validate before we move forward: 

1) Comparative probe: run NovusTech's prompt set (attached, sanitized) against Redwood's recommended serving config and the two hyperscaler endpoints we discussed (HyperscalerX-chat-v2, CloudGen-llm-3). Focus on: hallucination rate on factual QA prompts, answer accuracy on the labeled subset, latency p50/p95, and cost per 1M tokens.

2) Regression / stability checks: run 3 repeated batches across different seeds to check for variance in hallucination and token-level divergence. Highlight any prompt classes where responses degrade.

3) Deliverables: short write-up (1–2 pages) with method, raw metrics, example failure cases, and a recommended configuration for production (model variant, quantization, batching settings).

We attached the sanitized requirements doc and a small seed set (1k prompts). We'd like an initial canary (500 prompts) within 5 business days and a full run in ~10 business days if possible. Also include estimated cost and any commercial constraints (usage limits, reserved capacity needs).

Please loop in engineering for the evaluation plan. Happy to provide a signed EULA/NDA if needed for the larger dataset.

—Elena
Elena Soto
Head of ML Engineering, NovusTech
elena.soto@novustech.com

Attachments: novustech_requirements.pdf (doc), seed_prompts_sample.csv (csv)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@novustech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-10 11:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up + asks

Elena — really appreciate the clear ask and the sample prompts. We can run the comparative probe and the regression checks you describe. Proposed immediate plan: 

- Canary (500 prompts) within 3 business days.
- Full probe (1k prompts) + 3-repeat regression run within 9 business days.

Quick owners (internal): Marissa will manage scheduling and commercial terms; Rishi will own evaluation design and metrics; Vivek will run the benchmark on our infra and the hyperscaler endpoints. I'll coordinate results + customer write-up.

For the evaluation, we'll measure:
- Hallucination rate (we'll use your labeled subset for ground truth),
- Exact-match / semantic accuracy on QA pairs,
- Latency p50/p95 (client-configured concurrency),
- Cost estimate normalized to 1M tokens,
- Output variance across seeds (regression).

We propose one Redwood config to test initially: redwood-3b-q (int8-friendly) with prefix caching enabled and batching target of 8 tokens per request to emulate your latency constraints. We'll also run hyperscaler baselines with default recommended configs. If you can confirm the hyperscaler endpoints and any auth for them, we'll schedule the canary.

Attached: demo-recording.mp4 (internal recording for reference).

On the commercial side, Marissa — can you prep a short note on what a one-off evaluation engagement would cost vs reserved capacity?

Ben
Ben Carter
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

> On Sep 10, 2028, at 09:12, Elena Soto <elena.soto@novustech.com> wrote:
> > Ben — thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap and the things we'd like Redwood to validate before we move forward:...

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-11 09:45 -0700
Subject: Internal: NovusTech probe — test plan & asks (please action)

Team — forwarding Elena's request and the commitments we made. Need Rishi and Vivek to finalize the test harness and give time estimates. Key points to include in the test plan (drafted below):

Test plan (high level)
- Datasets: use Elena's supplied labeled subset (1k) and the 500-canary subset she approved. We'll also generate adversarial paraphrases (Rishi) to stress hallucination.
- Models/configs:
  * Redwood: redwood-3b-q (default), redwood-3b-fp16 (optional)
  * HyperscalerX-chat-v2 (baseline)
  * CloudGen-llm-3 (baseline)
- Metrics: hallucination_rate (defined as: asserted fact contradicting ground truth on factual prompts), semantic_accuracy, exact_match, p50/p95 latency, tokens_per_response, cost_per_1M_tokens. Set hallucination threshold for acceptance at <= 1.5% on the labeled factual subset.
- Regression checks: run 3 repeats with different RNG seeds; report mean + std. Highlight prompts with >10% variance in hallucination across seeds.
- Statistical significance: bootstrap 1k samples for confidence intervals on hallucination delta between Redwood and each hyperscaler.
- Output artifacts: raw outputs, token-level logs, small write-up (recommended config + examples).

Infra & scheduling
- Estimate compute: one dedicated GPU node (A100-class) for ~6 hours for full 1k x 3 repeats; canary ~45 minutes. Vivek — confirm resource needs and earliest slot.

Action items (owners)
- Rishi: finalize eval script, prepare eval-seeds.csv, and the hallucination adjudication rubric (due 2028-09-13).
- Vivek: reserve infra + run hyperscaler baseline connectivity checks (due 2028-09-14).
- Marissa: prepare pricing note for a one-off evaluation and any reserved-capacity pricing we should offer (due 2028-09-13).
- Ben: coordinate with Elena, schedule canary once infra & scripts ready.

Competitive positioning notes to include with the results (for the write-up)
- Measure latency with and without prefix/KV cache to show our caching win on repetitive prompts.
- Highlight dynamic routing to cheaper variants if latency SLOs can tolerate a slight quality delta.
- Include cost-per-token comparisons normalized for identical sequence lengths and batching.

Attachments: eval-seeds.csv (will contain the 500-canary list and the 1k labeled indices).

Please ack and update timelines in-thread.

—Ben

Ben / team — thanks, this looks good. Confirming: 

- Canary (500 prompts) by 2028-09-15 is fine.
- Full run and write-up by 2028-09-20 is acceptable if your infra estimate holds.

One additional ask for the deliverable: include a short section that explains any failure modes where Redwood's outputs might diverge from hyperscalers (e.g., tokenization differences, truncation behavior, or safety filters). We want clear examples we can show internal stakeholders.

I'll upload the full labeled test set to the Drive link (https://drive.google.com/novustech/test-data) and will send any required auth for the hyperscaler endpoints by EOD.

Also: please include a row in HubSpot for the evaluation engagement so our procurement can reference it — HubSpot link: https://hubspot.example.com/deal/9842.

I'll get legal to fast-track a limited-scope EULA; procurement will follow up with Marissa.

Thanks — Elena
